newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran to raise oil exports to China to 100,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Iran to raise oil exports to China to 100,000 bpd.

text.p: Iran will boost its oil exports to China by 43 percent to 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) over the next two years under an agreement signed on Sunday, Iranian television said.

The agreement was signed by Chinese Vice Premier Li Lanqing and Iranian Deputy President Mohammad Hashemi in Tehran on Sunday, said the television monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC).
Li met President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Sunday and "voiced Beijing's readiness to further develop economic and technical cooperation" with Iran, Iran's official news agency IRNA said.

"President Rafsanjani expressed pleasure with the growing trend of Tehran-Beijing cooperation and said close cooperation between the two countries would serve to consolidate (the) peace and stability of the region," IRNA said.

The television said that apart from boosting Iranian oil exports to 100,000 bpd from 70,000 bpd, the two sides agreed to complete several joint projects in Iran, including a cement factory, and on the transfer of satellite communication technology.
The two sides also reached agreement to increase cooperation in shipbuilding, fisheries and transport, it said.
China, which has angered Washington with its Iranian military ties, hopes to sell more missiles to Tehran, a Chinese industry official said in March.
Chai Zhongzhong, assistant to the president of missile builder China National Precision Machinery Import and Export Corporation, said China was only interested in selling defensive weapons to Iran.

The United States has voiced concern over Chinese sales of missiles and related technology to Iran, possibly in violation of the Missile Technology Control Regime, a 31-nation pact designed to head off missile proliferation.
U.S. officials say Iran has in the past two years tripled the number of missiles deployed on its Gulf coast and is fitting Chinese-built cruise missiles to 20 of its naval boats.
